why:
the publisher BUILDER (`node.publisher(topic).typed::<M>().qos(..).build()`) -- RFC-0022's `clone` tier, beside the `fork`-tier `create_publisher` that mirrors rclrs's shape. rclrs has one constructor and expresses the knobs as `IntoPublisherOptions`; ours is a builder because the knobs that matter here are TYPES, not values -- `.typed::<M>()` against `.generic(type, hash)` picks the entity's storage and its receive path, and a const-generic buffer bound cannot travel through an options struct. Both tiers are public and both are supported; `nros::` leads with rclrs's shape (phase-483; issue 0784, resolved).

On `nros::Node`, the executor-borrowing node handle (`exec.node_mut(id)`); it was `NodeCtx` until phase-483 W2, which the correlator folded onto `Node` (`TYPE_SYNONYMS`). MEASURABLE ONLY SINCE 2026-09-12: `nros_node::executor`'s `mod node` kept the type private while `Executor::node_mut` returned it, so every method on it was callable and none of them had ever produced a row -- issue 1351.
